theater: 出雲國雲門郡（島根縣雲南）

battle.name: 磐井之亂
battle.theater: 出雲國雲門郡（島根縣雲南）
battle.brief: 527年四月，出雲國雲門郡的忌部氏首領磐井別當舉兵，抗拒朝廷禁止其渡海攻略朝鮮南部的詔令。朝廷調伊勢、尾張及二十餘國舍人兵二萬討平，蘇我馬子宿禰大臣主持鎮壓，磐井別當敗退備中國後自刃。卡面羅馬標槍並未到過此戰場，它標示的是同類投射兵器：半米長、中空槍桿、專為折斷敵盾。

kit.name: 羅馬標槍
kit.history: 半米長的投槍，槍幹中空。捅穿盾之後就折斷，敵人只能帶著半截槍退回掩體。

countries: 磐井之亂是倭王權與出雲地方首長之間的一場內戰，交戰方大致分成兩塊。朝廷一方以大和的王權為核心，由在位天皇下詔，實際主持軍務的是蘇我馬子宿禰大臣一系；出兵的編制分三層，其一是伊勢、尾張兩國為主的中部諸國兵，其二是自二十餘國徵發、以近侍出身的舍人兵，其三是蘇我、物部等中央豪族自帶的部曲與騎士。磐井一方以出雲國雲門郡的忌部氏首領磐井別當為核心，據雲南、大田一帶的渡場與山地，向石見、伯耆、備前、備中方向拉開，並吸納沿線的國造與中小豪族部曲。依近年的整理，亂事另有另一種解讀：朝廷近江毛野率大軍準備渡海攻略朝鮮南部，筑紫國造磐井以九州方面的勢力加以妨害，最後由物部麁鹿火完成鎮壓。兩說的交戰主軸，一在出雲國司與朝廷的正面衝突，一在渡海主導權的爭奪，指向的卻是同一個問題，就是這片列島的航路與海權究竟聽誰的。
countriesEn: The Iwakuni rising was a civil war between the Yamato royal government and a provincial lord in Izumo, and the two sides can be described with some precision. The court side rested on the Yamato kingship, with the reigning emperor issuing the orders while Soga no Umako Suhune no Otomo actually directed the war effort. Its host was built in three layers: contingents raised mainly from Ise and Owari and the neighbouring provinces of the middle country; yado no hito, that is chamberlains, drawn from more than twenty provinces and enrolled as personal retainers of the court; and the private bands and mounted retainers of central clans such as Soga and Mononobe. On the Iwai side stood Iwai no Beto, head of the Kifune clan and of the Izumo provincial office, based at Unmon district around Unnan and Oda, with influence reaching along the coast towards Iwami, Hoki and the two Bingo provinces, drawing in local kokuzukuri and lesser clans with their private bands. A more recent reconstruction reads the affair differently: the court, under Keno no Mono of Omi, meant to launch a campaign against the southern Korean peninsula; the Tsukushi no Kimi Iwai obstructed that crossing from his base in Kyushu; and it was Mononobe no Okaji who finally put the revolt down. In either reading the real question was the same: who would control the sea lanes of this archipelago.
people: 史書留下姓名的核心人物只有數位。磐井別當，忌部氏出身，是出雲國司家的當主，也是出雲毛利一系的祖先，傳統記載說他企圖率領部曲渡海、攻略朝鮮南部伽耶，朝廷遣使諷諭不從，遂舉兵。朝廷一方，蘇我馬子宿禰大臣是鎮壓的主導者，蘇我氏自此在中央的權位更上一層；《日本書紀》在用明紀留下用明元年四月的記載，又在繼體天皇紀留下同一事件的另一筆，兩處並存使得這場內亂有了兩個年次。近年的整理補上兩位關鍵人物：近江毛野是策動渡海出兵的一方首長，磐井與毛野同出忌部一系的庶支，關係密切；物部麁鹿火則是親手執行鎮壓、把亂事壓回本地的人物。此外，佐伯直耳一系的大和豪族在亂前亂後的處境歷來有兩種解讀，或謂其站在朝廷一方協助平亂，或謂朝廷藉亂局清洗舊族，而其本人於537年被藤原氏所殺，正是這段中央角力的伏線。忌部氏這一支的族人，則在亂後集體失去朝廷的信任。
peopleEn: Only a handful of names survive in the records. Iwai no Beto, of the Kifune clan, was the head of the Izumo provincial office and the ancestor of the Omi Mochi line; the traditional account says he gathered his private bands to cross the sea and raid the southern Korean peninsula, refused the envoys the court sent to reason with him, and rose in arms. On the court side, Soga no Umako Suhune no Otomo led the suppression, and the Soga position at the centre grew stronger as a result. The Nihon Shoki preserves one entry under the reign of Emperor Yomei for the fourth month and a second under the reign of Keitai, so the same rebellion carries two regnal anchors. Recent scholarship adds two further names to the cast: Keno no Mono of Omi, the man behind the planned crossing of the sea, whose kin relationship to Iwai ran through the lesser branches of the Kifune; and Mononobe no Okaji, who carried out the suppression in the field and drove the revolt back into its own country. The position of the great Yamato clans around the Kifune, above all the house of Saeki, has been read in two ways: either they helped the court put the rising down, or the court used the rising to purge the older houses. The killing of Saeki no Nari Mimi by the Fujiwara in 537 is the loose end of that struggle. The Kifune collectively lost the trust of the court in the aftermath.
kits: 卡面所配的羅馬標槍，公元前1世紀已定型為羅馬軍團的標準投射兵器：半米長、槍桿中空，命中盾牌後即折斷，讓敵人拖著半截槍退回掩體。這件兵器本身並沒有出現在東亞的戰場上，它在此卡所標示的是武器類型。同時代日本列陣所用的，是矢倉弓矢配合槍與投槍這類短兵，鹿威以銹鐵包莖作近身刺擊，一方破風則是南朝形式經由渡來使節帶入列島的單翼標槍。弓矢方面，和弓配中矢、大矢與上刺箭，矢鏃有骨、石、鐵之分；防具是大楯，並以大鎧、橘皮甲護身，腰佩直刃太刀與鹿威；兵具由武具庫按編制發給，糧秣為粟、稗、鹽、乾魚，由伊勢、尾張沿海轉運至出雲。舟船是此役的關鍵裝備：磐井準備造舟渡海，朝廷的追擊與封鎖同樣依賴沿海船隻與渡場的控制，誰能先把船造好、把渡場握住，誰就掌握了主動。
kitsEn: The pilum on the card had been settled as a standard missile of the Roman legion by the first century BC: half a metre long, with a hollow shaft that snapped after passing through a shield, so that the enemy had to drag away the broken half. The weapon itself never reached the battlefields of East Asia; what this card marks is a type. What Japanese formations of the same age used were arrows from the yumi and yatate, worked together with short spears and javelins; the shika no tsuka, its tang wrapped in iron, served for close stabbing; and the hasso-happu, the single-flanged spear of southern Chinese form, had been carried into the islands by envoys from the south. On the bow side, the war bow threw chu ya, o ya and the upper piercing arrow, with bone, stone and iron heads. Defensive gear was the large shield, backed by the o yoroi and the tsubame-tate armour, with a straight-edged sword and the shika no tsuka at the waist. Weapons were issued from the armoury according to the establishment of each unit; the food was millet, barnyard grass, salt and dried fish, carried up the coast from Ise and Owari to Izumo. Boats were the decisive equipment of this war: Iwai meant to build ships for the crossing, and both the pursuit and the blockade of the court depended on coastal shipping and control of the ferry landings.
tactics: 磐井方的動作起於籌備而不是接戰：先在雲門郡集結部曲、徵發糧秣、砍伐木材造舟，把雲南、大田一帶的渡場變成出發點，準備向半島南部出航，再以舟師護住登岸隊伍。朝廷的第一步不是用兵而是使臣，遣人到場責問並勸諭，別當不從，才正式下詔討平；兵二萬自伊勢、尾張與二十餘國舍人分批向西集結，走的是東海道與山陰道這兩條補給線，沿海諸國的兵乘船，內陸諸國的兵步行，兩路前後銜接。交戰時以弓矢齊射壓住對方陣腳，槍與投槍填空檔，盾手結陣護住射手，騎兵與豪族部曲的衝鋒用來割裂潰散的一方；熟悉山陰山地與內海潮流的地方兵在追擊段佔盡便宜，朝廷的遠征部隊則受制於糧秣供應與路途距離。磐井別當退入備中國境，在安道一帶被追兵合圍，與少數隨從同赴死地，抵抗至此終止。
tacticsEn: Iwai's side began with preparation rather than with battle. He first mustered his private bands in Unmon district, levied grain and salt, felled timber for ships, and turned the landing beaches around Unnan and Oda into a point of departure, intending to sail for the southern peninsula with the fleet covering the landing parties. The court's first step was not an army but envoys, sent to upbraid and reason with him; only when he refused did the order for a punitive expedition go out. The twenty thousand men were gathered westward in batches from Ise, Owari and the chamberlains of more than twenty provinces, moving along two lines of supply, the Tokaido for the interior and the Sanindo for the coast, with the troops of the coastal provinces travelling by boat and those of the inland provinces on foot, the two columns joining in turn. In contact the archers opened with volleys to pin the enemy's formation, spears and javelins filled the gaps, shields were closed up to cover the archers, and mounted men and the private bands of the great clans charged to split a formation that had already broken. The local troops, who knew the mountains of Sanindo and the tides of the Inland Sea, held every advantage in the pursuit, while the distant army of the court was held back by grain supply and by the length of the road. Iwai no Beto fell back into Bingo, was hemmed in near Ando by the pursuers, and died by his own hand with a few of his followers.
data: 可核對的數字主要來自《日本書紀》。朝廷出兵的總數記作兵二萬，這是文獻中最明確的一項；參與的舍人兵分自二十餘國，通常列舉伊勢、尾張、美濃、三河、遠江、越前、若狹、但馬、因幡、伯耆、越中、能登、越後、佐渡、出羽、陸奧、常陸、下總、武藏等地，說明這是一場以近侍兵為骨架的全國性總動員。磐井方的總數則沒有留下可靠記載，一般只說是集結當地部曲與依附豪族，規模在數千之譜，絕大多數沒有固定編制。懲罰方面，史書記朝廷誅其黨，並以餘黨賜出雲臣民為奴屬，數目在記載上互有出入，或稱數千、或稱數百，難以坐實。地理上，自大和到出雲雲門郡直線約五百五十至六百公里，再加上備中國的追擊行程，全程接近千里。528年11月鎮壓完成的時點出自近年的整理，與用明元年527年4月舉兵、繼體天皇紀二十一年一系的記載，共同構成同一事件的三個時間座標。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked come mainly from the Nihon Shoki. The total of the court army is recorded as twenty thousand men, the single most definite number in the text. The chamberlains were drawn from more than twenty provinces, customarily listed as Ise, Owari, Mino, Mikawa, Totomi, Echizen, Wakasa, Tajima, Inaba, Hoki, Etchu, Noto, Echigo, Sado, Dewa, Mutsu, Hitachi, Shimotsuke and Musashi, which shows a general mobilisation of the realm built on personal retainers. No reliable total survives for Iwai's side; the usual description is local private bands and the followers of dependent clans, on the order of several thousand, most of them without any fixed establishment. On the penalty side, the chronicle has it that the court executed the rebels and granted the survivors as serfs to the people of Izumo, the numbers there differing between passages, given now as several thousand and now as several hundred, and impossible to settle. Geographically the direct line from Yamato to Unmon in Izumo is roughly five hundred and fifty to six hundred kilometres, and with the pursuit into Bingo the whole march approaches a thousand kilometres. The date of November 528 for the completion of the suppression comes from recent reconstruction, and together with the rising in the fourth month of Yomei year one and the entry under the twenty-first year of Keitai it gives the same event three chronological anchors.
cause: 直接起因寫在《日本書紀》裏：磐井別當聚徒、造船、籌劃渡海，準備以舟師攻略朝鮮南部伽耶，朝廷派遣使臣前往責問並勷諭，別當不從，這道拒絕成了導火線，朝廷隨即下詔各國出兵討平。但把時間拉長，起因的根子在大和與出雲之間長久的結構性矛盾。忌部氏世代執掌出雲國司與宗廟祭祀，在地方上握有編制、徵發與祭祀的實權；朝廷對出雲的祭祀主導與人事安排一向敏感，蘇我、物部一系與忌部一系在中央祭祀權與對外方針上早有分歧。背景則是5世紀東亞的整體局勢：高句麗南下，帶方、樂浪一帶的秩序崩解，半島南部與列島之間的物資與使節往來越來越頻繁，誰能主導渡海、誰能取得半島的物資與航權，就成了地方首長爭取的關鍵理由；蘇我氏願以朝廷的名義出兵，毛野一系則把渡海視為可以居功的事業，這種國家與豪族對海權的不同計算，最終把出雲推上戰場。
causeEn: The immediate cause is set down plainly in the Nihon Shoki: Iwai no Beto mustered followers, built ships and planned a crossing, intending to carry an expedition by sea against the southern Korean peninsula; the court sent envoys to question and counsel him; he would not yield; that refusal was the spark, and the court issued the order for the provinces to raise armies and put him down. But lengthen the time scale and the cause lies in a long structural friction between Yamato and Izumo. The Kifune had held the Izumo provincial office and the shrine sacrifices for generations, and on the ground they exercised real power over the registers, the levies and the rites. The court was always sensitive about who directed the sacrifices of Izumo and who staffed them, and the Soga and Mononobe lines had long differed from the Kifune over ritual authority at the centre and over policy abroad. The wider background is the state of East Asia in the fifth century: Goguryeo moving south, the order in the Byangfang and Naktong regions coming apart, and the traffic in goods and envoys between the southern peninsula and the islands growing steadily. Whoever could lead a crossing, whoever could secure the goods and the sea lanes of the peninsula, had the strongest reason to fight for it. The Soga were willing to launch the expedition in the name of the court; the Keno line treated the crossing as a career worth having. That disagreement between the state and the great clans over who should hold the sea is what finally put Izumo on the field.
impact: 磐井之亂留下的東西比戰果更多。首先是蘇我氏的抬頭：鎮壓之功記在蘇我馬子宿禰大臣一系名下，此後蘇我氏在中央的地位更加穩固，6世紀上半葉得以先後擁立推古與淨御兩位天皇，最終捲入587年星目之亂與592年滅亡之局，說明中央權威的重心正逐步從豪族聯盟轉向可以被個人化的權力。其次是忌部氏的沒落：亂後朝廷對出雲祭祀的信任撤走，宗廟祭祀的職能不再由忌部氏獨自掌握，中臣氏開始分擔，磐井一系從中央名單上退出，地方國司家開始向九州與外國方向尋找出路。第三是國家的用兵方式：兵二萬的調度顯示律令之前的大和朝廷只有一條可靠路徑，就是把兵役壓在近侍與地方豪族身上，舍人制度因此被推到前台，往後律令國家重整兵制、整頓防人與屯倉的改革，都是對這次經驗的直接回應。對外則是半島政策的第一次挫敗，渡海攻略的嘗試被地方勢力擋下，日本與伽耶、百濟的往來並未中斷，只是改由商船與使節的規模進行；同時，這也是日本有文字記載以來第一次真正的內亂，倭王權從此不再只是列島諸部落的盟主，而是一個需要對內用兵、對外揚威的國家。
impactEn: What the rising left behind was larger than its battlefield result. First the elevation of the Soga: credit for the suppression was entered under the name of Soga no Umako Suhune no Otomo, and the clan stood firmer at the centre afterwards, able in the first half of the sixth century to place two emperors on the throne in turn, Pushyu and Mimei, before being drawn into the Sumi no ran of 587 and its own destruction in 592; the centre of authority was visibly moving from a league of great clans towards a power that could be personal. Second the ruin of the Kifune: the court's confidence in the sacrifices of Izumo was withdrawn after the rising, the ritual office of the shrine house ceased to be theirs alone and the Nakatomi began to share it, the Iwai line dropped off the central rolls, and provincial office houses began to look for a future towards Kyushu and abroad. Third the way the state fought: a mobilisation of twenty thousand shows that the pre-Ritsuryo Yamato court had only one reliable path, pressing the burden of service onto personal attendants and provincial clans, and the chamberlain system was pushed to the front; the later reforms of the Ritsuryo state in the conscription, the frontier guards and the storehouses answer that experience directly. Abroad this was the first setback for Korean policy: the attempt to cross the sea was blocked by local power, the traffic with the southern peninsula did not stop but shrank to the scale of trading ships and envoys. It was also the first true civil war in Japan's written history, and from that point the Yamato kingship was no longer merely the head of a league of island clans but a state that had to wage war at home and display its reach abroad.
result: 結果是朝廷完勝，但勝得不體面。磐井別當的舟師未能成行，渡海的計劃隨舉兵一同暴露；他本人在敗走中退入備中國境，於安道一帶被追兵合圍，與少數隨從同赴死地，部曲或死、或降、或散入山中依附其他豪族，沒能再集結。出雲的秩序由朝廷重新接管，國司的任命與祭祀的主導回到中央手中，忌部氏失去宗廟的職分，其在中央的政治生命就此終結；餘黨按律處置，一部分被誅，一部分被賜為出雲臣民的奴屬，出雲地方社會為此付出了慘重的代價。軍功方面，蘇我氏的中央影響進一步擴張，朝廷完成了對出雲與筑紫一線的控制；從不許渡海到由朝廷主導、限定目的地的出海，日本對朝鮮半島的政策在這場內亂之後換了一種做法，雖然換得慢，方向卻已定。另外必須記住的是，此役在文獻上留下兩筆重複記載，用明元年與繼體天皇紀各記一次，年份因此有527年與更早一系的不同換算，鎮壓完成的時點亦有528年11月之說；史家引用時必須交代自己採用哪一套年表。
resultEn: The result was an outright court victory, though a shabby one. Iwai no Beto's fleet never sailed, and the plan for the crossing was exposed along with the rising. He himself fell back into Bingo, was hemmed in near Ando by the pursuers, and died by his own hand with a few of his followers; his bands were killed, surrendered, or scattered into the hills under other clans, and never mustered again. The order of Izumo was taken back into court hands, appointments to the provincial office and control of the sacrifices returned to the centre, the Kifune lost their place in the shrine service, and their political life at the court ended there. The remnants were handled according to law, some executed and some granted as serfs to the people of Izumo, and the local society of that province paid dearly for it. In terms of credit the Soga influence at the centre grew further, and the court completed its hold on Izumo and on the line towards Tsukushi. In place of forbidding the crossing altogether, the court now led the expeditions itself and limited their destination: the policy towards the Korean peninsula changed method after this civil war, slowly but with its direction already set. One caution must be kept in mind. The event is recorded twice in the literature, once under Yomei year one and once under the twenty-first year of Keitai, so the year can be given as 527 or on an earlier reckoning, and the completion of the suppression is variously placed in November 528; anyone citing the episode has to say which chronology they are following.
